newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Luxembourg Cegedel confirms eyes telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg Cegedel confirms eyes telecoms.

text.p: Luxembourg's part-privatised electricity company Cegedel confirmed on Tuesday it was eyeing a possible move into telecommunications after shareholders approved a change in its statutes on Monday.
Cegedel spokesman Nestor Didelot said, however, any move would depend on the outcome of a debate within the Grand Duchy on liberalising telecoms and there were no concrete projects.

"We are a network operator. There might be synergies with communication activities and we are studying in which areas it could be useful to be present. But at the moment there is nothing concrete," Didelot told Reuters by telephone.
Luxembourg's parliament on Tuesday began a debate on how the country's telecoms sector might be liberalised in line with a European Union directive to open the sector to full competition.
Under the EU law, most countries will be forced to liberalise all telecoms services by January 1, 1998, although Luxembourg has asked to postpone full competition until 2000.
"First we have to wait and see what will be decided," Didelot said.
Didelot said the change in Cegedel's statutes would also allow the company to further develop its core electricity business away from just distribution.
Under an agreement with the Luxembourg government last year to renew its concession until December 31, 2007, Cegedel is committed to expanding its use of renewable energy sources.
The company has also signed a new co-generation power agreement with Goodyear Luxembourg to add to an already existing accord with Luxembourg's Du Pont subsidiary.
The new power plant, which was agreed 14 days ago, should come on stream in 1998, Didelot said.
Cegedel is due to announce 1996 results around June 10.
